home-remodeling.local_heading: A narrow island, salt on both sides
intro_paragraphs: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea is a narrow run of barrier island, ocean on one side and Intracoastal on the other, and most of its houses were built when that was considered plenty. Bel Air and Silver Shores are full of low-slung 1950s and 1960s homes with terrazzo floors, jalousie-era window openings and kitchens sized for a percolator. Terra Mar Island Estates has the canal lots and the dockage. The whole-home remodel here is usually the same brief: keep the roofline and the address, replace everything that touches water, air or wiring.

Your permit comes from the Town of Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Development Services Department, where the Building Division is staffed under contract by CAP Government and plan review happens electronically. Behind the town sits the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which administers the building code countywide, certifies the officials who inspect your job, and issues the interpretations that settle arguments. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so every window and door needs HVHZ product approval. There is no architects' board to clear here; low-rise zoning does the shaping, and variances go to the Board of Adjustment, which is the Planning and Zoning Board sitting in that role.

We have been building in South Florida for more than twenty years, with 150-plus remodels and additions delivered and every one of them permitted and inspected. On an island this narrow that experience shows up as logistics: staging that does not block a neighbor's driveway, dumpsters scheduled around season traffic on El Mar Drive, and crews who check in at the Terra Mar gate without a fuss. The scope is fixed in writing before demolition. A supervisor is on site every day. The same team answers for it from estimate through warranty.

scope_items.name: Finish carpentry and flooring
scope_items.desc: Terrazzo restored or replaced, popcorn ceilings gone, and custom millwork scaled to eight-foot mid-century rooms rather than borrowed from a two-story catalog.

scope_items.name: Kitchen and baths last
scope_items.desc: Both trades folded into the master permit set so waterproofing, stone and cabinetry happen once, in order, instead of three times in three phases.

faqs.q: Who actually issues my building permit in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea?
faqs.a: The Town of Lauderdale-by-the-Sea does, through its Development Services Department. The Building Division itself is staffed under contract by CAP Government, and applications, plans and comments move through an electronic plan review portal rather than a counter. Inspections are requested online or by email with a cutoff for next-day scheduling. We handle the submittals, chase the comments, and keep the inspection calendar so your project is not waiting on a phone call.

faqs.q: Why does everyone here mention the Board of Rules and Appeals?
faqs.a: It is the county layer that sits above every building department in Broward. BORA administers the Florida Building Code as amended for Broward, certifies building officials and inspectors across the county's municipalities, hears appeals of their decisions, and issues formal interpretations when a code section is genuinely disputed. You will never sit in front of it for a kitchen. It matters because the inspector at your job works from a countywide standard, which is easier to build to when your contractor knows it.

faqs.q: My house is in a flood zone. Does that cap what I can spend on a remodel?
faqs.a: It does not cap spending, but it changes what a big number obligates you to do. Federal substantial improvement rules compare the cost of your project against the value of the existing structure; cross the threshold and the whole building has to be brought into flood compliance, elevation included. On a barrier island sitting only a few feet above sea level, that analysis belongs at the front of the project, before drawings, not at permit intake.

faqs.q: Can I add a second story to a Lauderdale-by-the-Sea house?
faqs.a: Often, within limits. The town's zoning protects a low-rise character, with residential height measured in a small number of stories and feet rather than the open-ended envelopes you see elsewhere on the coast. So the question is usually not whether you can go up, but how much of what you want fits under the cap. We check zoning and structure together, early, so nobody pays an architect to draw something the code will not allow.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home remodel here cost?
faqs.a: Wide ranges are the only honest answer before a walk-through, because a finish-level refresh and a full gut with new mechanicals, impact glass and structural work are different projects wearing the same name. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with real allowances instead of a low opening number that grows. PGX is a high-end builder; we are seldom the cheapest bid, and clients hire us because the signed figure holds.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the wish list, the survey if you have one, and your questions. We answer plainly and put the scope in writing, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Kitchen remodeling in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, FL. The galley wall goes and cabinetry built for salt air comes in. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and real layout changes for Lauderdale-by-the-Sea kitchens, including the condo ones with a service elevator and a board. Permitted, inspected, and run by a licensed general contractor.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: Kitchens built for salt and company
intro_paragraphs: Two kitchen problems dominate this town. In the single-family blocks of Bel Air, Silver Shores and Terra Mar Island Estates, the original 1950s kitchen is a closed room at the back of the house with a window facing the neighbor, built when nobody entertained in it. In the boutique buildings along El Mar Drive and North Ocean Boulevard, the kitchen is a narrow galley wedged behind a wall that was never load-bearing but has always been treated as sacred. Both problems have the same fix: take the wall out and start over.

Plumbing, electrical, mechanical and usually structure all come into play, so the kitchen gets permitted through Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Development Services with inspections at each rough stage. Plans and comments go through the town's electronic review portal. If you are in a condominium, the association's approval comes before the town's: expect an architect's letter for anything structural, certificates of insurance for the contractor, sound-transmission rules for new flooring, and service-elevator windows that decide when your cabinets can arrive. Buildings three stories and up also live inside Florida's milestone inspection and reserve-study regime now.

We order cabinetry early and template stone after the boxes are set, which is the boring discipline that keeps a kitchen from arriving three weeks late and a quarter inch off. Appliances get their own circuits, hoods get ducted properly instead of recirculating into the room, and every joint that will ever see water is detailed before tile is ordered. The scope is fixed in writing, a PGX supervisor is on site daily, and the rest of your house is papered and taped like it belongs to somebody.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Priced line by line before anything is demolished, so you know what you are buying. These pieces come up in most kitchens here.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry sized for salt air
scope_items.desc: Made-to-order boxes and doors with finishes chosen to survive island humidity, sized to the ceiling you have rather than the one a catalog assumes.

scope_items.name: Islands and stone
scope_items.desc: Marble, quartzite or porcelain templated in place, with island framing engineered for the slab weight and any overhang somebody will eventually sit on.

scope_items.name: Taking out the wall
scope_items.desc: Load calculations, a sealed beam detail and a permit for opening a 1960s block kitchen into the living room where everyone stands anyway.

scope_items.name: Moving the appliances
scope_items.desc: Relocating range, refrigeration and sink where the layout wants them, with new drains, vents and dedicated circuits permitted and inspected rather than improvised.

scope_items.name: Light you can cook by
scope_items.desc: Layered task, ambient and cabinet lighting on separate controls, plus the panel capacity an induction range and a wine column quietly demand.

faqs.q: My condo board has to approve the kitchen. How does that work with the town?
faqs.a: Two approvals, in order. The association reviews first, usually wanting stamped drawings for anything structural, a licensed and insured contractor on file, and agreement on work hours, elevator use and debris routes. Once that is settled, the permit application goes to the town. Running them in parallel sounds efficient and rarely is, because a board condition can force a drawing change after the town has already reviewed it. We sequence the paperwork so you pay for one plan set.

faqs.q: Can the wall between my kitchen and living room come out?
faqs.a: Usually, and an engineer decides rather than a tape measure. Most mid-century houses in Bel Air and Terra Mar are concrete block with a poured tie beam, which means an opening is a beam-and-column problem, not an impossibility. Second-floor and condo walls need the same scrutiny for different reasons. We get the structure evaluated before design gets emotional, because it is far cheaper to move a beam on paper.

faqs.q: How long will I be without a kitchen?
faqs.a: Cabinetry lead time sets the schedule, not demolition. Custom packages are measured in months to fabricate, so we order them first and keep your kitchen working until the delivery date is real. On-site work for a straightforward kitchen commonly runs a couple of months; add structural openings, appliance relocations or a condo elevator schedule and it stretches. We publish the sequence in writing so you can plan your life around it.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a kitchen this close to the beach?
faqs.a: Proximity to the ocean does not change the permit answer; scope does. Move a drain, add a circuit, run a gas line or open a wall and the town requires permits and inspections. Swapping a dishwasher into an existing hookup does not. What the coast does change is specification: appliance finishes, hardware and hood components corrode fast a few hundred feet from salt spray, so we choose for the environment, not the showroom.

faqs.q: Where does the money actually go in a high-end kitchen?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow close behind, and the invisible third is everything inside the walls: new supply and drain lines, dedicated circuits, panel capacity and ducted ventilation. Selections swing the total more than square footage does, which is why we scope against a specification rather than a per-foot guess. Expect a fixed written number after a walk-through, and expect us to be candid if your budget and your reference photos disagree.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and the photos you have saved. You will leave with a real scope and a real number, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, FL | PGX
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Barrier-island bath remodels in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, FL: corrosion-aware fittings, tested pans, heavy glass on real blocking. (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs for Lauderdale-by-the-Sea homes and condos, built over flood-tested membranes, permitted through the town, and inspected before a single tile goes down.
intro_paragraphs: Bathrooms date a house faster than anything else, and on this island most of them were laid out in the 1950s and 1960s. A three-piece bath off a hallway, a tub nobody uses, and a window that vents straight into the neighbor's carport. Owners in Bel Air and Silver Shores solve it by annexing a closet or a small third bedroom and building an actual primary suite. In the condos along El Mar Drive the footprint is fixed, so the work goes vertical: better light, better storage, and a shower you do not step over.

Bathroom work in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea is permitted through the town's Development Services Department, with plumbing, electrical and mechanical inspections at rough-in before anything gets covered. That sequence is a feature, not a hurdle: it means someone verified the shower pan and the rough plumbing while they were still visible. Condominium owners add an association layer first, plus sound-attenuation requirements under new tile and coordination with a building that may be working through its own milestone inspection. Broward's countywide code administration under the Board of Rules and Appeals sets the standard your inspector applies.

The parts of a bath that fail are the parts nobody photographs. So the membrane gets flood-tested and left standing overnight before tile is ordered, slopes get checked with a level instead of an eye, and heavy glass hangs on blocking that was installed for it. Exhaust ducts to the outside, which matters more on a barrier island than it does inland, because the humidity here never really leaves. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, protected floors from the front door in. Licensed, insured and accountable under Lic. CGC1539072.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Every line is settled before demolition, because a bathroom is where surprises get expensive fastest. Here is what usually makes the list.

scope_items.name: A primary suite, finally
scope_items.desc: Combining a hall bath, a closet and a spare bedroom into a genuine primary suite, with the plumbing rough-ins and permits handled as one package.

scope_items.name: Waterproofing that gets tested
scope_items.desc: Sloped, membraned and filled with water overnight before anyone touches tile, with linear drains and curbless entries where the slab will cooperate.

scope_items.name: Stone, glass, freestanding tubs
scope_items.desc: Marble and quartzite sealed for daily use, frameless enclosures set on real blocking, and tub locations verified against what the floor can carry.

scope_items.name: Original supply lines out
scope_items.desc: Swapping galvanized supply and tired cast iron while the walls are open, which is the only moment that work will ever be cheap.

scope_items.name: Exhaust and daylight
scope_items.desc: A humidity-sensing fan on a duct that ends outdoors, obscured glazing where neighbors are close, and sconce light usable at six in the morning.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a 1950s slab house here?
faqs.a: Often yes, sometimes with conditions. On a slab, a curbless entry means recessing the pan, which can require cutting concrete and rerouting drain lines; whether that is practical depends on where your existing waste line runs and how much fall it has. When the structure genuinely will not allow it, a low-profile curb with a properly sloped pan gets you most of the look without a leak. We answer that question before you commit to the tile.

faqs.q: Does the town inspect a bathroom remodel, or is that only for big projects?
faqs.a: The town inspects bathrooms. Plumbing rough, electrical rough and mechanical work all get looked at before walls close, and there is a final. Lauderdale-by-the-Sea runs its Building Division under contract with CAP Government and takes inspection requests online, with a same-day cutoff for next-day visits. We schedule around the trade sequence so the job is not sitting idle waiting for a slot, and you end up with a permit history that survives a home inspection at resale.

faqs.q: My building is doing its milestone inspection. Should I wait to renovate?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but talk to the association before you order anything. Milestone inspections and structural reserve studies can trigger building-wide repair work, and if your stack, balcony or slab is on that list, the timing of your bathroom matters. Sometimes the smart move is renovating right after the building's work reaches your line. Sometimes it is going now and coordinating access. We will read the board's schedule with you rather than around it.

faqs.q: Why does salt air matter inside a bathroom?
faqs.a: Because the air moves through the house. A few hundred feet from the Atlantic, chrome pits, cheap hinges bloom rust, and unventilated moisture finds every unsealed joint. We specify solid-brass valve bodies and marine-grade or properly finished hardware, seal stone against the humidity, and make sure the exhaust actually reaches the outside rather than the attic. It is not exotic. It is the difference between a bath that looks new in five years and one that does not.

faqs.q: How should I think about budget for a primary bath?
faqs.a: Think in three buckets: what you see, what you stand on, and what you never see. Stone, glass and fixtures set the tone; waterproofing, new supply and drain lines, blocking and ventilation quietly consume a real share. A powder room and a full primary suite are not in the same conversation. We scope the space, price it in writing, and would rather lose a job on honesty than win one on a number we know will move.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Tell us what fails you every morning. We will scope it properly and quote it in writing, in English o en español.

home-additions.h1: More square feet, same small town
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, garage conversions and in-law suites in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, engineered for HVHZ wind loads, permitted through town Development Services, and built under daily supervision by a licensed general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Growing a house on a narrow island
intro_paragraphs: Nobody is making more land here. The town is only a few blocks deep between the Intracoastal and the Atlantic, and the lots in Bel Air, Silver Shores and Terra Mar Island Estates were platted for the one-story ranch houses that still sit on them. So additions in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea are careful projects: a rear extension pushing a family room toward the canal, a primary suite over an existing garage, a second story that trades attic for bedrooms. Owners here add on because they want the dock, the dive access and the walk to the pier, not a bigger commute.

Local rules get interesting the moment you add square footage. Setbacks, lot coverage and low-rise height limits get checked by Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Planning and Zoning before the town's Building Division reviews structure, and a variance means a quasi-judicial hearing before the Board of Adjustment, whose members are the Planning and Zoning Board sitting in that capacity. Structural drawings must satisfy the Florida Building Code as Broward amends it, with product approvals rated for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone on every new opening. If the flood analysis pushes you past the substantial improvement threshold, elevation requirements arrive with it.

Two decades of South Florida work and 150-plus remodels and additions delivered mean we know where additions actually go wrong: the joint between old footing and new, the roof tie-in that leaks in year three, and the months of a family living around a construction zone. We tie new foundations properly, match stucco texture and roof profile so the seam disappears, and keep the occupied half of the house sealed, powered and livable. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, one accountable team from the first sketch to the warranty.
home-additions.scope_intro: Every addition begins with a survey, an engineer and a zoning check, in that order. Then it usually takes one of these forms.

scope_items.name: Extending out the back
scope_items.desc: The back of the house opened into the yard, with footings, beams and the roof joint detailed together instead of solved on site.

scope_items.name: Second stories, checked first
scope_items.desc: Existing block walls and footings evaluated by an engineer before anyone draws, then an upper floor designed to fit the town's height limits.

scope_items.name: Carports brought inside
scope_items.desc: Converting carports and garages into insulated, conditioned rooms with impact openings and mechanical work permitted, so the space counts at closing.

scope_items.name: Guest wings with baths
scope_items.desc: A wing with its own bath, sitting space and small galley for family who stay for months, built to code so the house still reads as one.

scope_items.name: Structure you never see
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, reinforced tie beams and the strap-and-anchor connections an inspector will hunt for before anything above them gets closed in.

faqs.q: How high can I build in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea?
faqs.a: Lower than most of the coast, and that is deliberate. The town's zoning keeps buildings low-rise, with residential height stated in both stories and feet, and the town has held that character while taller construction went up on either side of it. Practically, a second story is often possible, but roof pitch, floor-to-floor heights and any rooftop equipment all have to live inside the cap. We verify the exact limit for your zoning district before drawings begin, not after.

faqs.q: What is the timeline on an island addition?
faqs.a: Plan in quarters, not weeks. Survey, design and structural engineering take time on the front end; permitting through the town adds more, and a zoning variance adds a hearing cycle on top. Construction for a meaningful addition typically runs several months, longer for a second story that opens the roof. A year from first conversation to finished room is a reasonable expectation for a substantial project. You get the sequence in writing at estimate time, with the dates that depend on the town clearly marked as such.

faqs.q: Will an addition trigger flood elevation requirements?
faqs.a: It can, and this is the question to settle first on a barrier island. If the cost of the improvement crosses the federal substantial improvement threshold relative to the structure's value, the entire building has to meet current flood requirements, which may mean elevating. On a low-lying lot near the Intracoastal that changes the whole economics of the project. We run the analysis early, with the town, so you are choosing between real options rather than reacting to a plan reviewer.

faqs.q: I live on Terra Mar. Is a gated island harder to build in?
faqs.a: Different, not harder. Terra Mar sits behind a bridge and a guard gate, so deliveries, dumpster swaps and concrete trucks need scheduling and a crew list that the gate has in advance. Staging space is tight and neighbors are close, so we keep the site tidy, work inside the hours the community expects, and route heavy loads once rather than five times. It is coordination, and coordination is a contractor problem, not a homeowner problem.

faqs.q: Should I add on or just buy a bigger house nearby?
faqs.a: If the address is the asset, add on. There are only so many lots on this island with a dock, ocean access and a five-minute walk to the beach, and you already own one. An addition buys the exact space you are missing without giving up the location or restarting your tax basis. It is still months of construction, so it rewards people who plan to stay. Before you spend a dollar on drawings, we will tell you plainly whether the lot and the code agree with the idea.

home-additions.cta_sub: Send the survey and the sketch, or just point at the yard. You get a straight read on zoning, structure and cost, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.local_heading: Living outside on a narrow island
intro_paragraphs: Outdoor space is the entire point of living here. A house in Bel Air or on Terra Mar Drive might be modest inside and spectacular out back, where the canal, the dock and the sunset over the Intracoastal do the work. Along El Mar Drive the outdoor room is a courtyard or a roof deck facing the ocean. The projects follow: a covered terrace with a real summer kitchen, a pergola that shades a pool without fighting the sea breeze, a paver driveway that finally drains, an outdoor shower that gets the salt off before anyone walks inside.

Outdoor projects in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea carry rules the interior does not. Structures need building permits through town Development Services, and the gas, water and electrical serving a summer kitchen need their own trade permits and inspections. Anything visible from the beach falls under coastal lighting rules during sea turtle nesting season, which runs from March into the fall, so fixture selection and shielding are design decisions rather than afterthoughts. Seawall and dock work brings in Broward County alongside the town, and county resiliency standards now set minimum elevations for new and substantially rebuilt seawalls.

Outdoor work earns the same discipline as indoor work, which mostly means refusing to guess. Pergola and pavilion footings are engineered for uplift and detailed with the connections an HVHZ inspector expects. Drainage is planned so a terrace sheds water away from the slab instead of toward the front door. Cabinetry, hardware and appliances are specified for coastal exposure, because equipment spec'd for an inland patio does not survive two summers this close to salt spray. Fixed written scope, a supervisor on site daily, and a job site your neighbors do not have to complain about.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One coordinated project, not four trades arguing in your driveway. Terraces, kitchens, shade structures and hardscape designed, permitted and built together.

scope_items.name: An outdoor kitchen worth using
scope_items.desc: Permitted gas, water and electrical runs, marine-grade cabinetry and counters that shrug off spray, built into the terrace instead of parked on it.

scope_items.name: Pergolas anchored for wind
scope_items.desc: Shade structures with engineered footings and uplift connections, sized so the sea breeze still reaches the house and the roofline still makes sense.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and hardscape
scope_items.desc: Pavers, shell stone and finished concrete laid with slopes and drainage worked out first, because standing water on a coastal lot never dries quietly.

scope_items.name: Exterior coatings and roofing
scope_items.desc: Exterior restoration coordinated with roofing so scaffolding goes up once, plus stucco repair and coatings chosen for wind-driven rain and constant sun.

scope_items.name: Turtle-safe exterior lighting
scope_items.desc: Shielded, low-mounted, long-wavelength fixtures for beach-facing elevations, so the terrace is usable at night and the nesting-season rules stay satisfied.

faqs.q: Do turtle lighting rules really apply to my backyard?
faqs.a: If light from your property reaches the beach, yes. Broward's coastal communities, Lauderdale-by-the-Sea included, enforce lighting rules through nesting season, which runs from March through October. The standards are practical: mount fixtures low, use the fewest lumens that do the job, shield the source so it is not visible from the sand, and choose long-wavelength lamps. We design terrace and pool lighting to comply from the start rather than retrofit it after a code visit.

faqs.q: My seawall is old. Who has to approve replacing it?
faqs.a: More than one agency, which is why seawalls surprise people. The town permits the construction, and Broward County's environmental permitting side reviews work in tidal waters, sometimes with state involvement depending on scope. Broward has also adopted resiliency standards setting minimum elevations for new and substantially rebuilt seawalls on tidally influenced waterways, phased over the coming decades. If your wall is failing, plan the replacement as its own project with its own schedule, not as a line item on a patio job.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a pergola or an outdoor kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes, on both counts, and usually more than one. The structure needs a building permit; the gas line, water line and circuits each need their trade permits and inspections. Footings get engineered for wind uplift because Broward sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone and an unpermitted shade structure becomes a projectile in the wrong storm. Insurance carriers and future buyers also ask. We pull everything as one coordinated package rather than piecemeal.

faqs.q: What materials actually survive this close to the ocean?
faqs.a: Fewer than the showroom suggests. Within a few blocks of the Atlantic we specify marine-grade stainless or powder-coated aluminum rather than ordinary steel, dense stone sealed and re-sealed on a schedule, hardware rated for coastal exposure, and cabinetry built for weather rather than merely sold as outdoor. Fasteners matter as much as finishes; the wrong screw will stain a new travertine deck within a year. Specifying correctly once is cheaper than replacing cheerfully twice.

faqs.q: How much does an outdoor living project run?
faqs.a: It scales with utilities and structure more than with square footage. A paver terrace and a covered outdoor room with a plumbed summer kitchen, gas, water and dedicated circuits are different budgets entirely, and appliance and stone selections move the number as much as size does. We walk the yard, look at drainage and access, then price a written specification. If a phased approach fits your plans better, we will lay out sensible phases instead of pretending everything must happen at once.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Show us the yard, the dock and the list you keep adding to. We will come back with drawings, a specification and a price, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: A small town desk, a countywide code
intro_paragraphs: Most permit trouble in Lauderdale-by-the-Sea arrives with the deed. A title search flags an open addition permit on a Bel Air ranch, pulled by an owner two sales ago. An appraiser asks about the enclosed carport on Poinciana Street that appears in no town record. A lender pauses a refinance on Terra Mar Island Estates because a dock, a boat lift and a whole-house generator went in with no inspection anyone can find. The house is sound. The seawall is fine. The file is the problem.

Filing runs through the Town of Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Development Services Department, whose Building Division is staffed under contract by CAP Government. Drawings go up electronically, comments come back the same way, and inspections are requested online or by email against a daily cutoff. On top of the town sits the county's building code authority: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals publishes the Broward amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the plans examiner and inspector on your job, and rules on disputed readings. Broward is also High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window, door and roof system needs an approved product with its anchoring detail attached.

Twenty-plus years of South Florida work and more than 150 remodels and additions, every one permitted and inspected, add up to an unglamorous specialty: reading other people's records. We order the permit history before quoting anything, open up what has to be seen, and bring in the licensed engineer, architect or surveyor a file calls for rather than pretending to be one. Flood elevation gets checked early on a barrier island, because crossing the substantial improvement threshold changes the whole project. Inspections are booked by us and met on site by the supervisor who ran the job. Nothing here runs on a shortcut.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: What gets filed, and what gets fixed
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some of this is filed before a project starts. The rest is filed because a previous owner left it undone. Both begin with reading the record.

scope_items.name: The reroof that never finaled
scope_items.desc: Ordering the town's full permit history for the address, matching it against what is actually built, then reactivating, correcting or re-inspecting each one until the file closes.

scope_items.name: Work that was never filed
scope_items.desc: Enclosed carports, added baths, swapped windows and garage conversions that never reached the town: drawn as built, engineered where structure is involved, inspected against current code.

scope_items.name: HVHZ approvals and anchoring
scope_items.desc: Impact windows, doors and roof systems matched to approvals valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone and fastened exactly as the approval specifies, with the documentation attached.

scope_items.name: Inspections, in the right order
scope_items.desc: Rough, framing and final called in a sequence the job can actually meet, with someone from PGX at the door when the inspector shows up, so the permit closes.

scope_items.name: Repairs the report calls for
scope_items.desc: Concrete restoration, railings, waterproofing and electrical work that a milestone report or Broward's county safety inspection puts on an association's list, permitted and inspected together.

faqs.q: There is an open permit on my Lauderdale-by-the-Sea house and we close next month. What now?
faqs.a: Start with the record, not the repair. The town's file will show every permit ever pulled on that address, which inspections were signed, and exactly where things stopped. What comes next depends on what that shows. A missing final on sound work is the short version. Work that does not match the approved drawings is a longer one, and may need a licensed engineer to document what is actually there. Either way this runs in weeks rather than days, so make the call well before the closing date.

faqs.q: What actually needs a permit in a town this small?
faqs.a: More than owners expect. Structure, roofing, windows and doors, electrical, plumbing, gas and mechanical all do, and so do fences, pools, driveways, docks, lifts and seawalls, which on this island is most of what people want to change. Paint, flooring over a sound slab and a like-for-like cabinet swap generally do not. The items that quietly go unfiled are the ones that cost the most later: a carport enclosed into a room, a panel upgrade, a water heater moved, a shower added to a garage.

faqs.q: The contractor who pulled my permit is gone. Can PGX take it over?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. A permit is tied to the license that pulled it, so when that contractor disappears the job cannot simply be finished by someone else on the same paperwork. The town has a process for a qualified contractor to take over an existing permit, which means we become answerable for what was built before we arrived. That is why we look first: nobody puts a license behind concealed work they have not seen. Where something has to be opened up to be verified, we say so first.

faqs.q: Our oceanfront building has a milestone inspection report. Does PGX do that work?
faqs.a: The report is signed by a Florida-licensed engineer or architect; we bring that professional in rather than claim the title. State law requires milestone inspections for condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more: a visual first phase, and a second phase only where substantial structural deterioration turns up. Near salt water a local official can require the first one sooner. PGX does the repair scope that follows: concrete restoration, railings, waterproofing, electrical, permitted and inspected. The structural integrity reserve study runs on its own track.

faqs.q: What does it cost to clear an old permit problem?
faqs.a: That depends entirely on what is behind the wall. A missing final on work that was built properly is a small item. A room framed with no engineering behind it, or a roof installed without approved products, can mean opening it up and rebuilding to today's code. Permit fees are set by the town and scale with the value of the work, so they are not ours to mark up. What you get from us is the record read, a written scope, and the bad news early.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Give us the address, or the permit number if you have it. We will read the file and put the fix in writing, in English o en español.
